Decision: Use a single monorepo
Context: Keep applications, workers, contracts, domain packages, database assets, tests and infrastructure under one versioned repository.
Rationale: Atomic changes and contract visibility outweigh independent repository autonomy at the current team scale.

Decision: Use pnpm workspaces
Context: Manage JavaScript/TypeScript packages through a strict workspace-aware package manager.
Rationale: Fast deterministic installs and explicit workspace dependencies.

Decision: Use Turborepo task orchestration
Context: Coordinate build, lint, type-check and test pipelines across the monorepo.
Rationale: Provides dependency-aware task execution and cacheable CI work.

Decision: Use Next.js App Router for the web application
Context: Implement student, instructor and administrative experiences in one governed web application with clear feature boundaries.
Rationale: Matches the approved stack and supports server-side access checks.

Decision: Use TanStack Query for client server-state
Context: Use a dedicated query cache only where client-side revalidation is needed.
Rationale: Separates server state from local UI state and provides controlled invalidation.

Decision: Use React Hook Form plus schema validation
Context: Standardise accessible form state, validation and server error mapping.
Rationale: Avoids custom form frameworks and duplicated validation plumbing.

Decision: Use PostgreSQL as the transactional source of truth
Context: All canonical transactional state remains in managed PostgreSQL.
Rationale: Supports relational integrity, transactions, RLS and temporal audit.

Decision: Use SQL-first migrations
Context: Schema changes are version-controlled migration files reviewed with application changes.
Rationale: Prevents schema drift and keeps physical design explicit.

Decision: Use Supabase Auth behind an identity adapter
Context: Authentication uses the approved provider without leaking provider-specific identity concepts into business domains.
Rationale: Preserves portability and isolates authentication concerns.

Decision: Use Supabase Storage behind a media adapter
Context: Store restricted media in private buckets and expose only authorised signed access.
Rationale: Matches the approved platform while preserving an abstraction boundary.

Decision: Use a PostgreSQL-backed durable queue initially
Context: Run long jobs through a durable queue with retry and dead-letter support.
Rationale: Reduces new infrastructure while providing transactional integration.

Decision: Introduce Redis only for proven needs
Context: Use Redis for distributed rate limits, locks or high-value caching only after measured justification.
Rationale: Avoids premature cache inconsistency and operational cost.

Decision: Use a provider-neutral AI gateway
Context: All AI calls pass through typed provider adapters and governed model/prompt registries.
Rationale: Prevents vendor lock-in and centralises controls.

Decision: Use OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation
Context: Emit traces, metrics and structured context through a vendor-neutral standard.
Rationale: Allows observability backend changes without reinstrumenting domains.

Decision: Use transactional outbox events
Context: Commit domain changes and outbound event records in one database transaction.
Rationale: Prevents lost events and dual-write inconsistency.

Decision: Use REST-style command/query contracts
Context: Expose explicit versioned business APIs rather than generic table CRUD.
Rationale: Supports authorization, idempotency and business semantics.

Decision: Use OpenAPI as the public contract description
Context: Generate and validate API clients and contract tests from an approved API specification.
Rationale: Creates a cross-team source of truth.

Decision: Use feature flags for controlled rollout
Context: New capabilities, models and risky migrations are enabled by environment, academy or cohort.
Rationale: Supports gradual exposure and rollback.

Decision: Use immutable publication manifests
Context: Every academic publication records exact content, rules, approvals and version identities.
Rationale: Provides reproducibility and safe correction.

Decision: Use Playwright for end-to-end browser testing
Context: Automate critical student and operations journeys across supported browsers.
Rationale: Provides reliable cross-browser workflow tests.

Decision: Use Vitest for TypeScript unit and integration tests
Context: Standardise fast TypeScript testing across web and worker packages.
Rationale: Reduces tooling fragmentation.

Decision: Use contract-tested domain events
Context: Every event has a versioned schema, compatibility policy and consumer contract tests.
Rationale: Prevents asynchronous integration drift.

Decision: Use server-authoritative examination time
Context: All deadlines and validity decisions derive from server timestamps.
Rationale: Protects integrity across clock drift and browser manipulation.

Decision: Use private-by-default media access
Context: Files are inaccessible unless a domain permission grants a short-lived access mechanism.
Rationale: Protects student data and premium academic content.
